comparison: Both address the core finding of excess ancient polymorphisms (C2, C23-C29). OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED with robust statistical significance and appropriate controls. Peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN, requesting robustness checks for demographic model assumptions and analysis excluding CpG sites to rule out recurrent mutations.

Both evaluate the categorization methodology (C31-C34). OpenEval finds it SUPPORTED with validation from independent age estimation methods. Peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN, requesting more justification for the LD-based classification criteria and whether deletions truly share breakpoints.

Both address age estimation validation (C35-C37). OpenEval finds the concordance between categorization and age estimates provides strong validation (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN, noting that ages are for SNPs in LD rather than deletions themselves and requesting clarification on how accurate this proxy is.

Both evaluate balancing selection enrichment (C3, C38-C41). OpenEval finds it SUPPORTED with strong statistical significance and appropriate methodology. Peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN, requesting estimation of how many deletions are truly novel balancing selection loci versus simply linked to previously identified SNV loci.

Both address functional enrichment (C6, C42-C43). OpenEval finds it SUPPORTED with appropriate statistical testing and conservative definitions. Peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN, requesting additional evidence to strengthen the functional enrichment conclusion and the '27%' statement in the abstract.

Both evaluate phenotypic enrichment for immunity and metabolism (C44-C45). OpenEval finds it SUPPORTED with statistically significant and biologically plausible results. Peer reviewers also rate it SUPPORTED, raising no specific concerns about this analysis.

Both address allele frequency variation and mechanisms (C4-C5, C55, C70, C75-C77). OpenEval finds it SUPPORTED with strong statistical significance, though notes alternative mechanisms remain somewhat speculative. Peer reviewers also rate it SUPPORTED, requesting additional binned analysis to confirm findings but not challenging the conclusion.

Both evaluate functional effects and adaptive significance (C46-C50, C67-C69). OpenEval rates it UNCERTAIN, noting solid observational data but substantial speculation about adaptive significance. Peer reviewers rate it SUPPORTED, raising no concerns about these functional characterizations.

Both address differential selection on deletions versus SNVs (C8, C51, C63-C66). OpenEval finds it SUPPORTED with coherent evidence and appropriate statistical tests. Peer reviewers also rate it SUPPORTED, accepting the logic that stronger negative selection explains the lower proportion of ancient deletions.

Both evaluate size distribution patterns (C52-C54). OpenEval finds the paradoxical pattern (smaller median but larger tails) SUPPORTED as evidence for balancing selection on specific large deletions. Peer reviewers also rate it SUPPORTED, asking about length distributions but not challenging the findings.

Both address recommendations for future studies (C74). OpenEval finds it SUPPORTED as a logical follow-up from observed excess of large ancient deletions. Peer reviewers also rate it SUPPORTED within their broader acceptance of the size distribution analysis.

Both reference differential sharing patterns with archaic hominins (C30). OpenEval includes this as part of the converging evidence for ancient polymorphisms (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers also rate it SUPPORTED, raising no concerns about this observation.

OpenEval evaluates basic dataset characteristics (C58-C60) as SUPPORTED, including liftover validation that deletions are derived in humans. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these descriptive statistics.

OpenEval evaluates the phylogenetic reasoning about shared polymorphisms implying ancestral polymorphism (C61-C62) as SUPPORTED based on well-established population genetics principles. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval evaluates background knowledge and established literature (C1, C10-C22) as SUPPORTED, including divergence times and functional impacts. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these framing claims.

OpenEval evaluates the overarching conclusion (C9) synthesizing identification and functional relevance of ancient deletions as SUPPORTED by collective evidence. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this summary claim.
